title: Irish Channel dance jobs with Kid Punch's band and leaving in 1922
summary: He played tough Irish Channel dances with Kid Punch, walked there with his drums, and quit around 1922 for Tom Anderson's; drummer Chinee is discussed.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Huh? You ever work in the channel much?

Yeah, I played a lot of dance with... Well, later on in the year I played in the channel a lot with Kid Punch and Bang. Yeah, Kid Punch and Bang. Yeah, Kid Punch and Bang. Quiet, quiet? Was it quiet? No, no, them Irish's, man. They're tough, man. Them people. Oh, them is tough. In those days, those people is tough, man. They start a fight, man. Woo, woo. Never knew when that fight was gonna end, man. Gee, where is it?
What did you do when the fight stopped? When the fight stopped?

Just get out the way, move out the way. Try and protect my drums and get out the way. Well, they never bothered us. I mean, they'd be fighting amongst themselves. But they was good people, though. They were really nice. I played a lot of jobs up there with Kid Punch's band, Irish Channel. Kid Punch had so much work. At that time, I had to carry my drums, you know, from down here and all the way up to the Irish Channel. You see, you wouldn't lie on a street car. Or you'd catch a ride, somebody, you know, with a wagon or float was going up and I asked them, you know, give you a lift, you see. And sometime when we played, Irish Channel, I'd have to leave. The job was for 8 o'clock. Well, I'd put my drums on my back at 5 o'clock in the evening to get there for 8. I'd walk way up in Carlton, way up in Carlton, way up in St. Charles. You know, protection and everything, you have jobs like that. And I had a bass player, whoever the bass player was, I mean, at that time, we'd walk together. We'd meet one another. Who was the bass player? Gabe. A fella called Gabriel. We called him Gabe. I think he's still around. He was a Bob, I don't know. Tell me he's still around, I haven't seen him. And he was a hard workin', hard workin' bass player. Work hard all the time, Gabe. That's a good band we had. Ada Morris and the band Trombone, Punch. I don't know, Georgia Boyd. I can't think, Preston. Preston played the band, that's right. And Gabe played the bass. They had so many jobs, until I quit the band. I got a job going at Tom Anderson in 1922. Yeah, it was 22, I think it was 22. And I quit the band. I had too much work. I said, Ty Kennedy's just punch. And I think, I think it was Leroy replacement. I think it was Leroy Evans.
When did Chani play with Punch? Before you or after?

Oh, I don't remember. At that time Punch, Chani was playin' with Papa Salisbury. At that time, yeah. He must have played after, maybe afterwards. That's a guy who had a big reputation. Don't know how he could go back at it. He played good drums. What Chani would be? Oh, he was a good drummer.
He was a good drummer. I don't understand it. He's sick.
Huh? He's sick. He's sick now.
Yeah, he's sick now. He came up with us.
He was raised in the same neighborhood.
Yeah, raised in the neighborhood. Yeah.
Did he start out about the same time as you?
